title: Joining Whiteman on the road and enlarging old Goldkette arrangements
summary: Challis joined in Boston, roomed with Jimmy Dorsey and rewrote his Goldkette arrangements for the large Whiteman instrumentation.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

Anyway, it turned out fine. Bix played one of his best choruses, and the saxophone chorus was terrific. So I went around to the Paramount and got in touch with Whiteman and he said, 'Okay, we go up to Boston and so be there and go up with us,' so he said, 'Don't worry about doing any arrangements; just get acquainted with the guys in the band and what we do.'
So I joined the band and went out on the road with them. Went to Boston and I think Charlie Margulis joined us soon and Jimmy and Tommy were there, Charlie and let's see --

MR. CHALLIS: Charlie Margose. Shulvret Farrar went with Shulper so I got acquainted with the guys, you know, and kidded around and Jimmy and I became, we were roommates. We went out and Jimmy, you know, was very fine for me to have him in my corner. I -- he's the guy I think that got me in the band and when we roomed together, why we went around to these different towns and he knew everybody there, he had been around and played all around, and he took me around, you know, to some of these places, meet a lot of guys and then on the road, with the Whiteman band, I took some of the old Goldkette arrangements that I had made like Sugar and Sometimes I'm Happy, Just like a Butterfly and a few more things and made them out for the Whiteman band.

Yes, enlarging it which I always liked to do, so I filled them all out. My God, I used the eight saxophones with a little bass in there. It was brutal, it was just like making a hog of myself with all these instruments. I was pigging it. So we spent about ten weeks that way, there were ten weeks before we come into Chicago and at that time we were going to have a recording date there, going to do some recording, so the time was not yet right to get tunes or anything. So, Jimmy had his car on the road and Curt Dieterle one of the fiddle players, he drove Whiteman's car and Jimmy had to have his car which was a former Whiteman car and he and I would take -- would start about the last day the band would be in and we'd drive to the next town, and boy, I saw a lot of the country that I don't see however I would otherwise see it.

And we went through a lot of college towns and it was in the fall, beautiful. And in the meantime, I didn't hear much from the guys in the band and I just figured they went their separate ways and that the most of them had gone with the New Yorkers with Adrian Rollini.
